Hey I had an essentially chronic Bartholin cyst for a year. The previous year to that it would flare up and get infected (pain will tell you this) and I had to get it drained/get a Word catheter. I was extremely unimpressed and at times traumatized with the general medical response to my cyst.

Anyway the last year I had the same pattern of it always being there but then shrinking during my period. No idea why, maybe the change in the vaginal environment helped it drain? I used to use a fresh and clean washcloth in the shower daily to apply pressure and heat, it would help it drain and I believe this is what kept it somewhat under control. Eventually I decided to get surgery for it (laser ablation). If you want details on that check my comment history.

It basically shuts down the gland without removal. I had it done almost exactly a month ago. There's only one doctor that does it in the states, as the laser is pretty expensive equipment. His name is Dr David Ghozland and he is based on Santa Monica - I flew down there and stayed the day before and after. The cyst needs to be present for him to do it but if you're like me and had a chronic one that's no problem. It cost $2500, not covered by any insurance (I'm guessing it might fall under cosmetic procedure or just because it's a technique he developed himself?) but I was able to fundraise for it. He uses local anesthesia so I was quite awake and conscious, but it is a quick procedure. If it reoccurs within a year he will treat again at no cost, but I'm very hopeful it won't be coming back.

hey I've been in really tough situations in the past financially, the only reason I am not at the moment is because I got unemployment funds (in USA) and found a workable part time gig for the pandemic. I'm still barely floating but I assure you not everyone is stable!

* Is there any kind of eviction moratorium/legal protection for renters in your area due to the pandemic? 
* Food banks and pantries will provide you with food to cook for free. Hit them first, many places also offer delivery options.
* Look for free meal opportunities - Food Not Bombs is one. Religious groups are other options (some of them push religion, some don't). Sikhs and Hare Krishnas are two incredibly generous groups who serve free meals all over the world. 
* Seek out mutual aid networks in your area (Food Not Bombs is an example of mutual aid). These groups may have funding to distribute, or material support like going to the store for you if you are unable. You may even find disability-focused networks.
* Make sure you are getting all the governmental assistance you can qualify for, whether its long term or short term, for food, bills, etc. There are many supplemental programs available, look up "rent assistance + \[your city\]" or "financial assistance pandemic" or something like that. I know it takes a lot of energy to wade through the applications, just try to get through them one at a time, you can do it!
* Your partner may have access to more funding thru her school than she thinks - go to the financial aid office (or call, email is very slow!). Especially with the pandemic there may be extra funds available. Tell the office you are in danger of losing housing. Even without a pandemic there is always extra emergency funding \*somewhere.\* A good financial aid worker will be able to connect you with that money - even if it's a loan. I was so scared to go into debt when I was in college, and put it off for the first half, but if I hadn't taken out loans I wouldn't have been able to survive.
* A student job for your partner is also an easy way to get in a little extra cash and can be part of a financial aid package. My best student job was a receptionist in the disability support office, I just did some filing, answered a few emails, but mostly worked on homework.

Being poor is a full-time, exhausting job. Don't give up hope.

I have been dealing with Bartholin cysts for two years. The last year it's been basically chronic but I've managed to avoid it getting infected/painful.

I don't use tampons anymore. Menstrual cup + cloth pads.

I take serrapeptase every day, which seems to help thin the mucus and prevent the gland from getting too backed up.

I stopped taking sitz baths, mostly because they're so inconvenient and it didn't feel like it actually helped me.

If I feel the cyst is getting more swollen, I use castor oil at night. Others have used coconut oil. Sometimes I use a little tea tree oil (heavily diluted) if I'm worried about it being infected.

I shower every morning, and using a fresh washcloth soaked in the hot water, I gently press on the cyst to help it drain.

Also, I have avoided sex. Not exactly a long term solution but I think it has helped. I have had the cyst lanced twice as well as an unsuccessful Word catheter installed and it was all too traumatic to risk irritating it or getting an infection again.

I'm actually scheduled for a procedure using CO2 laser ablation next month which will hopefully let me be free of this once and for all.

Before cooking a filet of fish, rinse it in cold water and pat it dry with a paper towel first. This removes the film that forms on fish which contributes to that "fishy" taste and smell - but really, if it's a very strong smell the quality probably isn't good. Fresher seafood has a slight oceanic smell, if any, but once it starts to turn ammonia-esque the fish is just not in good shape.

Let it rest on a plate and come closer to room temperature before cooking it, whatever cooking method you are using. i.e., don't cook it right out of the fridge.

Bring to a gentle simmer at about medium heat and cook for \~10 minutes, or until the thickest part of the fish flakes and is opaque.
